ITQAN:v4p446/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p446/r2.speaker: المراكشي
ITQAN:v4p446/r2.claim: Al-Marrakushi says omission of waw in these four forms signals an action's speed and ease for its agent and its forceful effect on its object.
ITQAN:v4p446/r2.anchor: قال المراكشي السر في حذفها من هذه الأربعة التنبيه على سرعة وقوع الفعل وسهولته على الفاعل

ITQAN:v2p566/r38.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p566/r38.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p566/r38.claim: الزبانية is said to be plural of زبينة, زابن, or زباني.
ITQAN:v2p566/r38.anchor: الزبانية جمه زبينة وقيل زابن وقيل زباني

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after Abu Jahl challenged the Prophet while he prayed and boasted of his powerful assembly, the verses threatening to summon the guards were revealed; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p232#2/r4.anchor: فقال أبو جهل إنك لتعلم ما بها ناد أكثر مني فأنزل الله ﴿ فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال الترمذي حسن صحيح

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.claim: When no one else volunteered, Ibn Masʿūd offered to recite Sūrat al-Raḥmān to Quraysh; the Prophet initially feared for the small, weak Companion but eventually permitted him.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r1.anchor: روى) أنه لما نزلت سورة الرحمن ، قال عليه السلام : "من يقرأها على رؤساء قريش فتثاقلوا" فقام ابن

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd recited at the Kaaba; Abu Jahl slapped him, tearing and bloodying his ear, and he returned in tears while the Prophet grieved.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r2.anchor: فافتتح قراءة السورة فقام أبو جهل فلطمه فشق إذنه وادماها فانصرف وعينه تدمع فلما رآه عليه السلام رق قلبه

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.claim: Gabriel laughed at Ibn Masʿūd’s distress and said he would see what happened; at Badr, the Prophet sent Ibn Masʿūd to finish wounded survivors for a share in the reward of fighters.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r3.anchor: فإذا جبرائيل جاء ضاحكا مستبشرا فقال يا جبرائيل تضحك ويبكى ابن مسعود فقال سيعلم فلما ظفر المسلمون يوم بدر

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd found Abu Jahl alive and speared his neck from a distance, fearing he might still have strength; the author associates this with the later branding threat.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r4.anchor: فإذا أبو جهل مصروع يخور فخاف أن تكون به قوة فيؤذيه فوضع الرمح على منحره من بعيد فطعنه ولعل هذا قوله سنسمه على الخرطوم

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.claim: Too weak to climb Abu Jahl’s chest, Ibn Masʿūd used a ploy; Abu Jahl called him a shepherdling, and Ibn Masʿūd replied that Islam prevails and is not prevailed over.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r5.anchor: لم يقدر أن يصعد على صدره لضعفه فارتقى عليه بحيلة فلما رآه أبو جهل قال له يا رويعي الغنم لقد ارتقيت مرتقى

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.speaker: أبو جهل
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.claim: Abu Jahl told Ibn Masʿūd to tell Muhammad that no one had been more hateful to him, even at death.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r6.anchor: فقال له أبو جهل بلغ صاحبك إنه لم يكن أحد أبغض إلى منه في حال مماتي

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.claim: The Prophet called Abu Jahl more defiant than Pharaoh, who at least professed belief, while Abu Jahl only increased in arrogance.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r7.anchor: فروى أنه عليه السلام لما سمع ذلك قال فرعوني أشد من فرعون موسى فإنه قال آمنت وهو قد زاد عتوا

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd cut off Abu Jahl’s head with his blunt sword, could not carry it, cut the ear, tied on a cord, and dragged it to the Prophet; Gabriel joked that it was ear for ear, though the head too was severed.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن مسعود اقطع بسيفي هذا لأنه أحد وأقطع فلما قطع رأسه لم يقدر

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.claim: Abu Jahl once challenged Muhammad while he prayed and boasted that he had the largest council in the valley; the answer threatens him with the punishment angels.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r14.anchor: روى أن أبا جهل مر برسول الله وهو يصلي فقال ألم ننهك فاغلظ رسول الله فقال أتهددني وأنا أكثر أهل الوادي ناديا يريد كثرة من

BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r15.claim: Zabāniya are torment angels who will drag Abu Jahl to Hell; one can overpower a million of his council.
BURSEVI:v10p366#2/r15.anchor: {سندع الزبانية} أي ملائكة العذاب ليجروه إلى النار وواحد منهم يغلب على ألف ألف من أمثال أهل ناديه.

BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.claim: The Prophet said that if Abu Jahl summoned his council, the torment angels would have been called into view.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r1.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "لو دعا ناديه الزبانية عيانا".

BURSEVI:v10p367/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r2.claim: The Uthmanic codices all omit the wāw in sandaʿ; grammatically it is not required, perhaps omitted for parallelism with falyadʿu or because the call is as inevitable as a command.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r2.anchor: اجتمعت المصاحف العثمانية على حذف الواو من سندع خطا ولا موجب للحذف من العربية لفظا ولعله للمشاكلة مع فليدع أو للتشبيه بالأمر

BURSEVI:v10p367/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r3.speaker: ابن خالويه
BURSEVI:v10p367/r3.claim: Ibn Khālawayh says the underlying form is sandaʿu; the wāw drops before the still lām, and Qurʾanic spelling follows pronunciation in comparable forms.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r3.anchor: ابن خالويه في إعراب الثلاثين آية الأصل سندعو بالواو غير أن الواو ساكنة فاستثقلها اللام ساكنة فسقطت الواو

BURSEVI:v10p367/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r4.claim: Zabāniya in ordinary Arabic means police or guards, a marked group of rulers’ aides; singular zubniya derives from pushing because they violently drive unbelievers into Hell.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r4.anchor: والزبانية في الأصل في كلام العرب الشرط كصرد جمع شرطة بالضم وهم طائفة من أعوان الولاة سموا بذلك لأنهم أعلموا أنفسهم بعلامات يعرفون بها

BURSEVI:v10p367/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r5.claim: Lexicographers give singular forms zubniya or zubnā and explain the ending by alteration or replacement of the yāʾ with tāʾ.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r5.anchor: والواحد زبنية كعفرية وعفرية الديك شعرة القفا التي يردها إلى

BURSEVI:v10p367/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p367/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p367/r6.claim: In the inward reading, forceful majestic manifestations drag Abu Jahl, the commanding soul, and the dark forces of his council—his desires—toward the fires of abandonment and loss.
BURSEVI:v10p367/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى التجليات القوية الجلالية الجرارة أبا جهل النفس الأمارة وأهل ناديه الذي هو الهوى

QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.claim: Let him summon his council; God will summon the Zabaniya and command them to destroy him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p436/r17.anchor: فليدع أهل ناديه وأهل مجلسه ، وسندعو الزبانية ونأمرهم بإهلاكه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the one who forbids prayer as Abu Jahl, the 'assembly' as his clan, and the summoned wardens as angels.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3450#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ارايت الذي ينهى عبدا اذا صلى قال : أبو جهل نهى محمدا اذا صلى فليدع نادية قال : عشيرته

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451/r1.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Harith says the wardens' feet reach the earth while their heads reach the sky.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3451/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحرث قال : الزبانية ارجلهم في الأرض ورؤوسهم في السماء

TUSTARI:96:18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:96:18/r1.claim: The zabaniya are keepers of Hell, with feet on earth and heads in the lowest heaven; their name comes from pushing, as they shove the damned from behind with hands and feet.
TUSTARI:96:18/r1.anchor: يعني خزنة جهنم، أرجلهم في الأرض ورؤوسهم في السماء الدنيا. وإنما سموا الزبانية من الزبن

TUSTARI:96:18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:96:18/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:96:18/r2.claim: When Abu Jahl heard of the zabaniya, he fled to his people and admitted he feared them though he did not know who they were.
TUSTARI:96:18/r2.anchor: فلما سمع أبو جهل ذكر الزبانية هرب إلى قومه، فقالوا له: أخفته؟

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl confronted Muhammad as he prayed at the Maqam, threatened him, and boasted that he had the largest council; the verses answer his threat to mobilize his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r3.anchor: ما رواه الترمذي والنسائي عن ابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.claim: The council is first the place where people assemble; it is called a council only while its members are gathered, and its daytime gathering contrasts with the nighttime “sāmir”.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r4.anchor: اسم للمكان الذي يجتمع فيه القوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.claim: Qusayy established a Quraysh council house around the Sacred Mosque for consultation and major affairs; the site was gradually incorporated into later mosque expansions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p450/r5.anchor: واتخذ قصي لندوة قريش دارا تسمى دار الندوة حول المسجد الحرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r1.claim: “We will summon” answers the taunting imperative and is jussive as its response; the muṣḥaf spelling omits the wāw and future prefix to strengthen the verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r1.anchor: فإن دعا ناديه دعونا لهم الزبانية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r2.claim: The word “zabāniya” has several proposed plural forms, or may be a plural collective with no singular of the same form; it derives from forceful pushing, and refers to punishment angels, while also naming police assistants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r2.anchor: بفتح الزاي وتخفيف التحتية جمع زباني بفتح الزاي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r3.claim: “Kalla” rebuts the challenge and confirms that Abu Jahl will not carry it out.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r4.claim: The muṣḥaf omits a wāw after the ʿayn in “we will summon,” because it is joined in recitation rather than paused at a verse ending.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p452/r4.anchor: في المصحف بدون واو بعد العين مراعاة لحالة الوصل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r2.claim: Zabāniya are the angels of punishment who push people into Hell; the singular may be zabniya, zabnī, or zābin, and the root means pushing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r2.anchor: والزبانية ملائكة العذاب واحدهم زبنية، وقال الكسائي زبني، وقال عيسى بن عمر والأخفش: زابن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r3.claim: Several poetic examples use zabn and zabun for pushing, including one describing war driving people back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r3.anchor: والزبن الدفع، ومنه حرب زبون أي تدفع الناس عن نفسها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r4.speaker: عتبة بن أبي سفيان
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r4.claim: Utba ibn Abi Sufyan says war pushed them and they pushed back, so they are children of war and war their mother.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r4.anchor: ومنه قول عتبة بن أبي سفيان: وقد زبتنا الحرب وزبناها فنحن بنوها وهي أمنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r5.claim: The written codex omits the wāw in sanadʿu for shortening; the meaning is that God will summon the guards to punish the caller of his council.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p503/r5.anchor: وحذف الواو من سندع في خط المصحف اختصارا وتخفيفا، والمعنى: سندع الزبانية لعذاب هذا الذي يدعو ناديه،

AKHFASH:v2p582/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r3.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p582/r3.claim: Some give zabānī as the singular of zabāniya.

AKHFASH:v2p582/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r4.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p582/r4.claim: Another says its singular is al-zābin, which al-Akhfash says he heard from ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar.
AKHFASH:v2p582/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "الزابن" سمعت "الزابن" من عيسى بن عمر

AKHFASH:v2p582/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r5.speaker: بعضهم
AKHFASH:v2p582/r5.claim: A further reported singular is zabaniya.

AKHFASH:v2p582/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p582/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p582/r6.claim: Because Arabs scarcely know a singular, he treats zabāniya as a plural with no singular like abābīl, indicating multitude like ʿabādīd and shaʿārīr.
AKHFASH:v2p582/r6.anchor: والعرب لا تكاد تعرف هذا وتجعله من الجمع الذي لا واحد له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet in prayer; after the Prophet rebuked him, Abu Jahl boasted of his clan, prompting the warning to call his assembly and the promise of the guards of Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p176#7/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل فقال ألم أنهك عن هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r1.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r1.claim: The zabaniya are stern, powerful angels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r1.anchor: قال عطاء هم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r2.claim: The zabaniya are the keepers of Hell.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r3.claim: In Arabic, zabaniya can mean the guards or police.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة الزبانية في كلام العرب الشرط

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r4.claim: Al-Farra says al-Kisa'i first knew no singular for zabaniya, then later proposed zabniya, though he was unsure whether this was analogy or received usage.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r4.anchor: كان الكسائي يقول لم أسمع للزبانية بواحد ثم قال بأخرة واحد الزبانية زبني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda gives zabniya as the singular and says it denotes any rebellious human or jinn.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة واحد الزبانية زبنية وهو كل متمرد من إنس أو جان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة وابن دريد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r6.claim: They derive the word from pushing: the guards push the people of Hell into it; the root also describes a camel pushing its milker and people jostling one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p179#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة وهو مأخوذ من الزين وهو الدفع كأنهم يدفعون أهل النار إليها قال ابن دريد الزبن الدفع

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.claim: Abu Jahl is challenged to summon his clan for help, while God will summon the angels of punishment to show which party prevails.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r1.anchor: {فليدع ناديه} أي: قومه وعشيرته، أي: ليدعهم يستنصر بهم، {سندع الزبانية} وهم ملائكة العذاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad's neck if he saw him pray at the Kaaba; the Prophet warns angels would seize him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن على عنقه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl confronting the Prophet at the Maqam and boasting of his large assembly; the verses were revealed, and Ibn Abbas says the angels would take him immediately if he called them. Al-Tirmidhi grades this hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل بن هشام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.claim: In another report from Ibn Abbas, Abu Jahl threatens to step on the Prophet's neck; the Prophet says angels would seize him visibly if he did. The report also warns that people challenging the Prophet would face loss.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت رسول الله يصلي عند الكعبة لآتينه حتى أطأ على عنقه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad for praying at the Maqam, verses about the forelock, his council, and the angels were revealed; the Prophet prayed and Abu Jahl saw troops between them. Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he moved.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p438/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه. فأنزل الله، عز وجل:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl swearing to trample Muhammad while he prayed; as he approached he recoiled, describing a trench of fire, terror, and wings. The Prophet says angels would have snatched him limb by limb; the narrator is unsure whether the revelation context was part of Abu Hurayra's report. Ibn Kathir says Ahmad, Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Abi Hatim transmit it through Mu'tamir.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قالوا: نعم. قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته يصلي

FARRA:v3p279/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p279/r3.claim: The zabāniya are stronger than the men summoned and work with hands and feet; a camel can repel and kick a milker.
FARRA:v3p279/r3.anchor: فهم أقوى وهم يعملون بالأيدي والأرجل، والناقة قد تزبن الحالب وتركضه برجلها.

FARRA:v3p279/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r4.speaker: الكسائي
FARRA:v3p279/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī later reported zabnī as a singular of zabāniya, but was unsure whether it was heard or inferred by analogy.
FARRA:v3p279/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي: بأخرة واحد الزبانية زبني وكان قبل ذلك يقول: لم أسمع لها بواحد، ولست أدري أقياسا منه أو سماعا.

FARRA:v3p279/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p279/r5.speaker: عبد الله
FARRA:v3p279/r5.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh adds ilā before nādiyah and uses fa-sa-adʿū for “then I will call.”
FARRA:v3p279/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله: «كلا لئن لم ينته لأسفعا بالناصية» ، وفيها: «فليدع إلي ناديه فسأدعو الزبانية»

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r1.claim: Qatāda says zabāniya are the police in Arab usage.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r1.anchor: قال قتادة: (3) "هم: الشرط؛ في كلام العرب".

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r2.claim: Others derive the word from zabn, pushing: they drive Hell’s people toward it; one of them is a zabaniyya.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p534#6/r2.anchor: غيره: "وهو من "الزبن" مأخوذ. و "الزبن": الدفع. كأنهم يدفعون أهل النار إليها. واحدهم: "زبنية".

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r7.claim: Zabn means forceful pushing; the Zabāniya are so named because they push Hell's inhabitants into it harshly.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r7.anchor: والزبانية: لأنهم يدفعون أهل النار فيها بشدة

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives zubniyya as the singular of zabāniya.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r8.anchor: واختلفوا في واحد الزبانية، فقيل: زبنية، عن أبي عبيدة،

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r9.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r9.claim: Al-Kisāʾī gives zabnī as the singular.

JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r10.speaker: الأخفش
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash gives zābin as the singular; other forms are zabānī or a collective plural like abābīl.
JISHUMI:v10p7479#2/r10.anchor: زابن، عن الأخفش، وقيل: زباني، وقيل: يجوز أن يكون اسما للجميع كأبابيل.

JISHUMI:v10p7482/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r3.claim: The Zabāniya are angels, named for their strength in pushing the people of Hell into it harshly.
JISHUMI:v10p7482/r3.anchor: هم الملائكة، عن ابن عباس، وقتادة، ومجاهد، والضحاك. سموا بذلك لأنهم لقوتهم يدفعون

KASHSHAF:96:18/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:18/r1.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF:96:18/r1.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads the verb in the passive: the punishment angels will be summoned.

KASHSHAF:96:18/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:18/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:18/r2.claim: In Arabic, zabaniya means guards or police, from pushing; its singular form and variant derivations are explained lexically.

KASHSHAF:96:18/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:18/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:96:18/r3.claim: The intended referents are the angels of punishment.

KASHSHAF:96:18/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:96:18/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF:96:18/r4.claim: The Prophet says that had Abu Jahl summoned his gathering, the angels would have seized him before his eyes.
KASHSHAF:96:18/r4.anchor: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عياناً

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r10.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r10.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads the verb in the passive: the guards will be summoned.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : ( سيدعى الزبانية ) على البقاء للمفعول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r11.claim: Zabaniya means guards in Arabic; its forms derive from pushing or repelling, and here it means angels of punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r11.anchor: والزبانية في كلام العرب : الشرط ، الواحد ، زبينة ، كعفرية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r12.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r12.claim: The Prophet says that if Abu Jahl summoned his council, the guards would seize him in plain sight.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p784/r12.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 1325 ) ( لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية

MAJAZ:v2p304/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p304/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p304/r6.claim: Zabāniya has singular zabniya; a rebellious human or jinn may be called a zabniya ʿifriya.
MAJAZ:v2p304/r6.anchor: «الزبانية» (18) واحدهم زبنية وكل متمرد من إنس أو جان يقال: فلان زبنية عفرية.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r4.claim: The zabaniya are angels guarding Hell, exceptionally large and forceful; Arabs also use the word for anyone fierce, as a poet's line illustrates.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p308/r4.anchor: والزبانية هم الملائكة من خزنة جهنم , وهم أعظم الملائكة خلقا وأشدهم بطشا , والعرب تطلق هذا الإسم على من اشتد بطشه

MUJAHID:v2p772#3/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p772#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p772#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says the zabaniya are angels.
MUJAHID:v2p772#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال الزبانية الملائكة

MUQATIL:96:9-19/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r6.claim: The zabāniya are more fiercely angry at Abū Jahl than Banū Makhzūm are at Muhammad; a Prophetic report pictures Abū Jahl dragged face-first over embers in Hell, regretting that he mistreated Muhammad and begging to return and make his clan believe.
MUQATIL:96:9-19/r6.anchor: فهم أشد غضبا عليه من بني مخزوم على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.claim: Nadi is the gathering place and means its people; zabaniya are the punishment angels, a word for enforcers derived from pushing.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r1.anchor: ﴿ فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية ﴾ النادى المجلس الذى يجتمع فيه القوم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.claim: A report says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet during prayer, the Prophet rebuked him, and Abu Jahl boasted that he had the largest assembly in the valley; the Prophet warned that the angels would seize him if he called them.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p349#11/r2.anchor: روى أن أبا جهل مر بالنبى عليه السلام وهو يصلى

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the zabaniah are harsh, forceful angels; lexical authorities give several singular forms and Qatada says the term means police in Arabic.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r2.anchor: أي الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد عن ابن عباس وغيره واحدهم زبني

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r3.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i gives zabni as the singular of zabaniah; al-Akhfash, Abu Ubayda, and other authorities offer zābin, zabniya, and zabani, or treat it as a collective.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش: زابن. أبو عبيدة: زبنية. وقيل: زباني.

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r4.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r4.claim: Qatada says zabaniah means police in Arabic and the word derives from pushing or shoving, as in muzabana in sales.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: هم الشرط في كلام العرب. وهو مأخوذ من الزبن وهو الدفع

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r5.speaker: أبو الليث السمرقندي
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r5.claim: Abu al-Layth al-Samarqandi reports that the angels are called zabaniah because they use their feet as they use their hands.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r5.anchor: حكاه أبو الليث السمرقندي رحمه الله قال: وروي في الخبر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r6.claim: A report says Abu Jahl threatened to summon his clan to protect him, then fled in fear after imagining a mounted angel threatening him with the zabaniah.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r6.anchor: وروي في الخبر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما قرأ هذه السورة، وبلغ إلى قوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r7.claim: Reports portray the zabaniah as having heads in heaven and feet on earth, pushing unbelievers into Hell; another view calls them the greatest and strongest angels, and the word can describe powerful people.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r7.anchor: وفي الأخبار أن الزبانية رؤوسهم في السماء وأرجلهم في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r8.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r8.claim: A poet describes powerful, generous fighters as zabaniah, supporting the word's association with great force.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r8.anchor: قال الشاعر: مطاعيم في القصوى مطاعين في الوغى

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r9.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r9.claim: Ikrima reports Ibn Abbas's story that Abu Jahl threatened to trample the Prophet, who said angels would seize him openly; al-Tirmidhi grades this report hasan, sahih, and gharīb.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r9.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس: { سندعو الزبانية } قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r10.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r10.claim: A second report says Abu Jahl confronted the Prophet at the Maqam, boasted that his clan was the largest assembly, and Ibn Abbas said the punishment angels would have seized him immediately; al-Tirmidhi calls it hasan, gharīb, sahih.
QURTUBI-FULL:96:17-18/r10.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال: مر أبو جهل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي عند المقام،

QUTB-ZILAL:96:18/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:18/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:18/r1.claim: God will summon the stern, harsh Zabaniya, so the outcome of the confrontation is already known.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:18/r1.anchor: أما نحن فإننا ( سندع الزبانية )الشداد الغلاظ

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.claim: Qutb suggests this may be the occasion when the Prophet seized Abu Jahl by the collar and rebuked him; Abu Jahl replied by boasting of his powerful council.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r3.anchor: وقال له : أولى لك ثم أولى فقال : يا محمد بأي شي تهددني

QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says that had Abu Jahl called his council, the angels of punishment would have seized him immediately.
QUTB-ZILAL:96:19/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس لو دعا ناديه لأخذته ملائكة العذاب من ساعته

RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.claim: While the Prophet prayed, Abu Jahl threatened him; his boast about having the largest gathering occasioned the summons of his assembly and the zabaniya, who would seize him if he summoned them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p18#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي فجاء أبو جهل

RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.claim: After the Prophet rebuked Abu Jahl and recited these verses, Abu Jahl boasted of his large assembly of dependents; this prompts the challenge to summon it and God's counter-summons.
RAZI-FULL:v32p24/r7.anchor: قال : يا محمد بمن تهددني وأني لأكثر هذا الوادي ناديا

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Mubarrad give zabaniya's singular as zabniya, from pushing; the word can describe a rebellious human or jinn, like ifriya.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والمبرد : واحد الزبانية زبنية وأصله من زبنية إذا دفعته

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r2.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash transmits zabani as one proposed singular; others propose zabin.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r2.anchor: وقال الأخفش : قال بعضهم واحده الزباني ، وقال آخرون : الزابن

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r3.claim: Another grammatical view treats zabaniya as a plural with no singular in the same form, like ababil and abadid.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : هذا من الجمع الذي لا واحد له من لفظه

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r4.claim: The intended beings are powerful angels of punishment; Muqatil describes them as Hell's keepers, with feet on earth and heads in heaven.

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r5.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r5.claim: Muqatil says the zabaniya are Hell's keepers, whose legs are on earth and heads in heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هم خزنة جهنم أرجلهم في الأرض ورؤسهم في السماء

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r6.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r6.claim: Qatada says zabaniya means police in Arabic and describes the harsh, strong angels who push unbelievers into Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة : الزبانية هم الشرط في كلام العرب وهم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r7.claim: The angels are called zabaniya because they push unbelievers into Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r7.anchor: ملائكة النار سموا الزبانية لأنهم يزبنون الكفار أي يدفعونهم في جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.claim: One reading dares Abu Jahl to call his supporters against Muhammad, while God summons zabaniya beyond his people's power; Ibn Abbas says they would seize him immediately, and other readings place his dragging in this world at Badr or in the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r8.anchor: الأول : أي فليفعل ما ذكره من أنه يدعو أنصاره ويستعين بهم في مباطلة محمد

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says that if Abu Jahl summoned his assembly, the zabaniya would seize him at once, visibly.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية من ساعته معاينة

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.claim: An alternative reverses the order: God will seize the forelock and summon the zabaniya in the afterlife, so Abu Jahl may then call his assembly to try to stop them.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r10.anchor: القول الثاني : أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا أي لنسفعا بالناصية وسندع الزبانية في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.claim: The fāʾ in ‘let him summon his assembly’ signals a miracle: the challenge invites the unbeliever to call them, which would trigger God's counter-summons; his failure to dare shows the Prophet's miracle.
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r11.anchor: الفاء في قوله : { فليدع ناديه } تدل على المعجز

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r12.claim: A passive reading, sutdaʿā, means ‘will be summoned’; this is certain divine action, especially as a promise to avenge the Prophet, and the future tense recalls the promise to help even after a time.

RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r13.claim: The reading is not an expression of uncertainty: God's promise is bound to occur, as the prophetic assurance says, ‘I will help you even after a while.’
RAZI-FULL:v32p25/r13.anchor: فائدة السين هو المراد من قوله عليه السلام : ( لأنصرنك ولو بعد حين )

SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses zabāniya as police; its singular may be zubniya from pushing, or a nisba form zabnī altered from zabānī; ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash give zābin, while others say it has no singular from its form.
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r1.anchor: الزبانية في كلام العرب: الشرط، الواحد زبنية كعفرية، من الزبن وهو الدفع

SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r2.claim: The root signifies pushing, as a cited poetic line calls warriors zabāniya; war is said to push people, and a customer is a zabūn as he is pushed from vendor to vendor.
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r2.anchor:
والحاصل أن المادة تدل على الدفع قال:
4610 مطاعيم في القصوى مطاعين في الوغى
زبانية غلب عظام حلومها

SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r3.claim: The common reading has the majestic plural sanadʿu, written without wāw like yadʿu al-dāʿ; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the passive sayudʿā al-zabāniya, with the angels raised as agent.
SAMIN-DURR:96:18/r3.anchor: وقرأ العامة " سندع " بنون العظمة ولم ترسم بالواو، وقد تقدم نظيره نحو: " يدع الداع

TAB:96:18/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r2.speaker: author
TAB:96:18/r2.claim: After Muhammad rebuked him for stopping prayer, Abu Jahl boasted of having the largest council; God answers that He will summon the zabāniya if he persists.
TAB:96:18/r2.anchor: لأن أبا جهل لما نهى النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الصلاة عند المقام ،   انتهره رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   وأغلظ له ،   فقال أبو جهل :  علام يتوعدني محمد

TAB:96:18/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad at the Maqam; the Prophet rebuked him, and Ibn ʿAbbas says angels would seize him if he called his group.
TAB:96:18/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام ،   فمرّ به أبو جهل بن هشام

TAB:96:18/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r4.claim: In another account, Abu Jahl says his council is greatest; the narrator does not remember Muhammad's reply, but Ibn ʿAbbas says angels would take him if he acted.
TAB:96:18/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي ،   فجاءه أبو جهل ،   فنهاه أن يصلي

TAB:96:18/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB:96:18/r5.claim: Abu Hurayra recounts Abu Jahl's oath to trample Muhammad, his sudden retreat before a trench of fire and wings, and the Prophet's warning that angels would seize him limb by limb.
TAB:96:18/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  هل يُعَفّر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم ؟

TAB:96:18/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad if he prayed again; black ranks appeared between them, and angels would have seized him had he moved.
TAB:96:18/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه ،   فأنزل الله

TAB:96:18/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:18/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that angels would have visibly seized Abu Jahl if he tried to trample the praying Messenger.
TAB:96:18/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة

TAB:96:18/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:18/r9.claim: Mujahid explains the zabāniya as angels.
TAB:96:18/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد {  سَنَدْعُ الزّبانِيَةَ } قال :  الملائكة

TAB:96:18/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r10.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي الهذيل
TAB:96:18/r10.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi al-Hudhayl describes the zabāniya as having feet on earth and heads in heaven.
TAB:96:18/r10.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي الهُذَيل :  الزبانية أرجلهم في الأرض ،   ورؤوسهم في السماء

TAB:96:18/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r11.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:18/r11.claim: Qatada says the Prophet warned that if Abu Jahl acted, the zabāniya angels would seize him in plain sight; Qatada glosses them as angels.
TAB:96:18/r11.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  {  سَنَدْعُ الزّبَانِيَةَ } قال النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «لَوْ فَعَلَ أبُو جَهْلٍ لأَخَذَتْهُ الزّبانِيَةُ المَلائِكَةُ عِيانا »

TAB:96:18/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r12.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:18/r12.claim: Qatada also identifies the zabāniya as angels.
TAB:96:18/r12.anchor: عن قتادة {  سَنَدْعُ الزّبَانِيَةَ } قال :  الملائكة

TAB:96:18/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:18/r13.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:96:18/r13.claim: Al-Dahhak also identifies the zabāniya as angels.
TAB:96:18/r13.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  الزبانية ،   قال :  الملائكة

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Abu Jahl’s threat, his sudden retreat from a trench of fire, awe and wings, and the Prophet’s statement that angels would tear him apart; the passage gives the revealed sequence.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، قال: قال أبو جهل: هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم؟ قال: فقيل: نعم، قال: فقال: واللات والعزى لئن رأيته

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the prayer place; when Muhammad prayed, Abu Jahl saw dark battalions between them and would have been seized by angels.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r2.anchor: عن الوليد بن العيزار، عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه، فأنزل الله:

TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl’s vow to trample the Prophet’s neck and the Prophet’s warning that angels would seize him visibly.
TAB-FULL:v24p539/r3.anchor: عن عبد الكريم، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: قال أبو جهل: لئن رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة، لآتينه

TAB-FULL:v24p540/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r2.claim: Mujahid says the zabāniya are angels.
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، {سندع الزبانية} [العلق: 18] قال: «الملائكة»

TAB-FULL:v24p540/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي الهذيل
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r3.claim: The zabāniya are described as having feet on earth and heads in heaven.
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي الهذيل: الزبانية أرجلهم في الأرض، ورءوسهم في السماء

TAB-FULL:v24p540/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r4.claim: Qatada reports the Prophet saying that if Abu Jahl acted, the punishment angels would seize him in plain sight.
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {سندع الزبانية} [العلق: 18] قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لو فعل أبو جهل لأخذته الزبانية الملائكة عيانا»

TAB-FULL:v24p540/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r5.claim: Qatada also directly glosses the zabāniya as angels.

TAB-FULL:v24p540/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise identifies the zabāniya as angels.
TAB-FULL:v24p540/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " الزبانية، قال: الملائكة "

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r10.claim: The zabāniya are angels assigned to Hell, stern wardens against whom human help will be useless.

TABATABAI:96:11-19/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r11.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:96:11-19/r11.claim: A further lexical view says zabāniya means policemen in the language of the people.

ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r7.claim: The zabāniyah are severe, stern angels, as described in 66:6.
ZAJJAJ:v5p345/r7.anchor: الزبانية الغلاظ الشداد، واحدهم زبنية، وهم ههنا الملائكة، قال الله

TABRISI:96:2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة والكسائي والأخفش
TABRISI:96:2/r7.claim: The singular of zabaniya is given variously as zabina, zabna, or zabin; the term derives from pushing, as a camel pushes its milker away with its leg.
TABRISI:96:2/r7.anchor: وواحد الزبانية زبينة عن أبي عبيدة وزبنى عن الكسائي وزابن عن الأخفش

TABRISI:96:2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:2/r8.speaker: الشاعر
TABRISI:96:2/r8.claim: An unnamed poet uses the verb zabana to mean that war would push or jolt someone.
TABRISI:96:2/r8.anchor: ومستعجب مما يرى من أناتنا ولو زبنته الحرب لم يترمرم

TABRISI:96:16-19/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:96:16-19/r5.claim: If Abu Jahl had called his council, the keepers of Hell would have seized him immediately in plain sight.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r5.anchor: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية النار من ساعته معاينة

TABRISI:96:16-19/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:96:16-19/r6.claim: Alternatively, the verse announces that God will summon the angels whether Abu Jahl calls his council or not; his death at Badr confirmed it.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r6.anchor: إخبار بأنه يدعو إليه الزبانية دعا ناديه أم لم يدع وصدق سبحانه ذلك

TABRISI:96:16-19/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:96:16-19/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:96:16-19/r7.claim: Zabaniya are the harsh, strong angels assigned to Hell.
TABRISI:96:16-19/r7.anchor: يعني الملائكة الموكلين بالنار وهم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

THALABI:v10p246/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p246/r6.claim: When Abū Jahl forbade prayer and was rebuked, he threatened to summon cavalry or footmen; the Prophet said the guards would take him openly.
THALABI:v10p246/r6.anchor: لأملأن عليك إن شئت هذا خيلا جردا أو رجالا مردا، فأنزل الله سبحانه فليدع ناديه أي قومه

THALABI:v10p246/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p246/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p246/r7.claim: The Prophet warned that the guards would seize Abū Jahl in full view.
THALABI:v10p246/r7.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «لأخذته الزبانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r1.claim: Zabāniya is plural of zabaniya, a forceful taker, from the verb meaning to push; it can name a rebellious human or jinn, like ʿifrīt/ʿafāriya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة (¬7)، (والمبرد (¬8)) (¬9): واحد الزبانية: زبنية، وهو الشديد الأخذ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash records proposed singulars al-zabānī, al-zābin, and al-zābiniya, but says Arabs barely recognize them and usually treat zabāniya as a plural without a singular.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r2.anchor: وقال الأخفش: قال بعضهم: واحدها الزباني، وقال بعضهم: الزابن، وقال بعضهم: الزابنية، والعرب لا تكاد تعرف هذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r3.claim: They are the assistants of Hell; even if Abū Jahl summoned his council, God's zabāniya would seize him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الأعوان زبانية جهنم (¬3). ووالله لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r4.claim: They are Hell's keepers, whose feet are in the earth and heads in the sky.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: خزنة جهنم أرجلهم في الأرض، ورؤوسهم في السماء (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r5.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r5.claim: Qatāda says zabāniya is the Arabic term for guards or police.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة: الزبانية الشرط (¬1) (¬2) في كلام العرب (¬3).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p180/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد (¬4).

WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r1.claim: The zabaniya are stern, forceful angels.
WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r1.anchor: { سندع الزبانية } وهم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r2.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r2.claim: The Messenger said that if Abu Jahl summoned his council, the zabaniya would seize him openly; no grading is stated.
WAHIDI-QT:96:18/r2.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عيانا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r1.claim: The zabaniya are stern and mighty angels.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r1.anchor: سندع الزبانية } وهم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r2.claim: The Prophet warned that if Abu Jahl called his assembly, the zabaniya would seize him in plain sight.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:96:18-19/r2.anchor: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عيانا

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r5.claim: Zabaniya names the punishment angels; lexicographers say the original word meant police or security forces, with disagreement over whether it has a singular form or derives from zabn, repelling.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r5.anchor: “Zebânî”, “Zebâniye” azab melâikelerine isim olmuştur. Demişlerdir ki asıl lügatta şurta, yani zâbıta kuvveti demektir

ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r6.claim: The summons of these angels implies that the lying, sinful person will be dragged into Hell.
ELMALILI:96:9-19#3/r6.anchor: Bu zebânîlerin davetinden anlaşılır ki o yalancı, cânî nâsıye cehenneme sürüklenecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r2.claim: Zabāniya is a plural from a root meaning to push or drive away and, as a religious term, means angels of punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r2.anchor: “itmek, savmak” anlamına gelen zeben kelimesinden türemiş çoğul bir isim olup dinî terim olarak azap meleklerini ifade eder

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.speaker: Rivayete göre
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.claim: After Abu Jahl threatened Muhammad while he prayed at Abraham's station and boasted of his many supporters, the verses challenged him to call his council while God would call the angels of punishment; he never dared act despite hearing them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:96:17/r3.anchor: Allah Teâlâ, “O hemen kurultayını çağırsın, biz de zebânileri çağıracağız” buyurarak Hz. Peygamber’e meydan okuyan Ebû Cehil’in yetersizliğini ortaya koymak istemiştir

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r1.speaker: عكرمة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r1.claim: The verses about Abu Jahl calling his assembly and God calling the guards were revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Abu Jahl tried to stop the Prophet praying, then boasted his assembly was largest; the verses followed, and Ibn Abbas says God's guards would seize him if he summoned it.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يصلي، فجاء أبو جهل

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that if Abu Jahl had called his assembly, God's guards would have seized him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p460/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: والله لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله تبارك وتعالى

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r1.claim: The traditional interpretation makes zabāniya hell wardens, but the word's meaning is uncertain; Jeffery proposes Syriac leaders or Persian flame, and Eilers suggests a Middle Persian word for jailers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Wird traditionell auf die Wärter der Hölle gedeutet; die Bedeutung ist jedoch unsicher

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r2.claim: An attestation in ancient Arabic poetry more convincingly identifies zabāniya as demon-like beings; an Ephrem parallel describes punishment angels dragging the condemned to hell.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r2.anchor: dass der Ausdruck zabāniya auch in der altarabischen Dichtung auftritt und dort dämonenartige Wesen bezeichnet

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r3.speaker: Jeffery; Eilers
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r3.claim: Jeffery links the word to Syriac guides of the dead or Persian flame; Eilers derives it from Middle Persian jailer, though the author considers such etymologies less convincing.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:18:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Jeffery will den Ausdruck mit syr. dāborē, den „Führern“, die Ephrem zufolge die Verstorbenen zum Gericht führen, in Verbindung bringen

CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.claim: The condemned is challenged to summon his earthly supporters against the punishment awaiting him, but God's summoned zabāniya outmatch that following.
CORPUSCORANICUM:96:15-18:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die von dem Getadelten zur Hilfe gerufene Anhängerschaft (nādiyahū) wird jedoch gleich darauf durch die von Gott herbeizitierten zabāniya überboten

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.claim: The verses challenge the arrogant to summon their faction while God summons His guards; Badr later demonstrated the Quraysh’s humiliation by God’s guards.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r1.anchor: the Quraysh was humiliated at the hands

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p391/r3.claim: Zabāniyah means defenders and can describe police or law enforcers; here it is a temporary divine task force of angels.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.speaker: النبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet said angels would seize Abū Jahl if he acted on his threat to trample the praying Muhammad.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾ قال قال أبو جهل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r3.claim: Qatāda says zabāniya is the Arabic word for the police.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p384#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ الزبانية ﴾ قال الزبانية في كلام العرب الشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r6.claim: Zabāniya are the angels of punishment; some say the plural has no singular of the same form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r6.anchor: الزبانية: ملائكة العذاب، فقيل: جمع لا واحد له من لفظه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives the singular as zabniya, modeled like ḥadriya or ʿafriya; al-Kisāʾī instead gives zabnī, reanalyzed as a nisba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r7.anchor: واحدهم زبنية على وزن حدرية وعفرية، قاله أبو عبيدة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r8.speaker: عيسى بن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r8.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash give zābin as the singular; the word also describes someone forceful, supported by poetry and ʿUtba ibn Abī Sufyān’s saying about war.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p505/r8.anchor: قال عيسى بن عمر والأخفش: واحدهم زابن، والعرب تطلق هذا الاسم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r18.claim: The majority read sanadʿu with an active nūn; the written wāw is omitted because it drops in connected speech when two vowelless letters meet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p511/r18.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سندع بالنون مبنيا للفاعل، وكتبت بغير واو لأنها تسقط في الوصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r6.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the verb passively, making al-zabāniya the nominative subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p512/r6.anchor: سيدعى مبنيا للمفعول الزبانية رفع. كلا: ردع لأبي جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r1.claim: The zabāniya are punishment-angels who drag Abu Jahl to Hell; the word originally denoted police or governors' aides, then forceful men generally, and the angels are named for pushing their victims.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r1.anchor: سندع الزبانية أي ملائكة العذاب ليجروه إلى النار وهو في الأصل الشرط أي أعوان الولاة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r2.claim: Lexicographers disagree on the singular: it may have no singular form, be zabniya, or be zabni; the plural is explained as deriving from a root meaning to push, with a changed form.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r2.anchor: واختلف فيه فقيل جمع لا واحد له من لفظه كعباديد وقال أبو عبيدة زبنية بكسر فسكون

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر والأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r3.claim: ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash give its singular as ibn; a cited poetic line uses zabāniya for powerful, imposing warriors.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r3.anchor: وقال عيسى بن عمر والأخفش واحده وابن والعرب قد تطلق هذا الأسم على من اشتد بطشه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r4.claim: A report says that if Abu Jahl had called his gathering, the zabāniya would have seized him visibly in this world.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r4.anchor: وهذا الدعاء في الدنيا بناء على ما روي من أنه لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عيانا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r5.claim: Sandʿu is indicative because it lacks a subjunctive or jussive governor; the written form omits wāw to match its spoken elision before a consonant, or to echo falyadʿu. Making it a jussive answer to the command is doubtful.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r5.anchor: والظاهر أن سندع مرفوع لتجرده من الناصب والجازم ورسم في المصاحف بدون واو لأتباع الرسم للفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r6.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r6.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads the verb in the passive and raises al-zabāniya as its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p188/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة سيدعي الزبانية بالبناء للمفعول ورفع الزبانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r2.claim: Zabāniya is a plural related to pushing or driving.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r2.anchor: سندع الزبانية} جمع زبني مأخوذ من الزبن وهو الدفع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the term means the guardians of Hell, named because they drive its people into it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد زبانية جهنم سموا بها لأنهم يدفعون أهل النار إليها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r4.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj identifies them as stern, powerful angels.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج: هم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.claim: If Abu Jahl called his clan, God's guards would seize him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p481/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r1.claim: The zabāniya drag the offender to Hell; the term's singular may be zabniya, from pushing away, or a nisba form whose tāʾ replaces yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r1.anchor: ليجروه إلى النار وهو في الأصل الشرط واحدها زبنية كعفرية من الزبن

BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.claim: A report promises the reciter a reward as though he had recited the entire set of shorter suras.
BAYDAWI-FULL:96:18-19/r4.anchor: من قرأ سورة العلق أعطي من الأجر كأنما قرأ المفصل كله

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.claim: The nadi is the group the deluded man summons for help; all of them are powerless against the mighty angels God summons to punish him.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r1.anchor: مراداً به الجمع الذين يدعوهم هذا الضال المغرور، وهو مظنه أن يؤازروه وينصروه

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r2.speaker: بعض اللغويين
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r2.claim: Lexicographers disagree on زبانية: some treat it as a plural without singular; Abu Ubayda gives زبنية, al-Kisaʾi زبنى, and al-Akhfash زابن, an active participle for fierce force.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r2.anchor: فقيل إنه جمع لا واحد له. وقال أبو عبيدة: واحده زبنية، وقال الكسائي، واحده زبنى

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r3.speaker: الأخفش
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash derives a singular زابن from zabn, meaning one of fierce attack; the author cites a poem and Utba ibn Sufyan’s phrase about war pushing and being pushed.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r3.anchor: وقال الأخفش. واحد الزبانية زابن، اسم فاعل من زبن، بمعنى اشتد بطشه

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r4.claim: Arabic uses زبانية for rebellious humans or jinn and also for a scorpion’s poisonous horns; religious usage makes them angels charged with tormenting sinners in Hell.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r4.anchor: ونقلت الزبانية إلى المصطلح الديني علماً على الملائكة والموكلين بعذاب الخاطئين في جهنم

BINTSHATI:v2p33/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r5.claim: The verse leaves the angels’ manner of punishment unspecified, allowing the imagination to range freely over its terror.
BINTSHATI:v2p33/r5.anchor: ولم تحدد الآية صنيع الزبانية، بل تركته على إطلاقه الرهيب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r3.claim: God will summon the zabāniya, Hell's appointed helpers who drag offenders there; the term originally refers to guards and those who push, and describes powerful, imposing beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r3.anchor: أي الأعوان الموكلين بالنار ليجروه إليها , وهم في الأصل الشرط

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r4.claim: The singular zabniya is explained through the root zabn, pushing, or as a nisba form whose tāʾ replaces yāʾ.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r4.anchor: الواحد زبنية كهبرية , من الزبن وهو الدفع أو زبني على النسبة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r5.claim: The Uthmānic codices omit the wāw in yadʿu; the author speculates this avoids attributing independent elevated strength to the angels, or makes their summoning certain and irresistible, or shows that the slightest call suffices.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p487/r5.anchor: وقد اجتمعت المصاحف العثمانية على حذف الواو من هذا الفعل خطأ

DURR:96:6/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:6/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:6/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:6/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:6/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies Abu Jahl as forbidding Muhammad’s prayer, glosses his nadi as his clan, and says al-zabaniya are angels.
DURR:96:6/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل نهى محمداً إذا صلى { فليدع ناديه } قال : عشيرته { سندع الزبانية } قال : الملائكة

DURR:96:6/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:6/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن الحرث
DURR:96:6/r12.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Harith describes the zabaniya as having their feet on earth and their heads in heaven.
DURR:96:6/r12.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحرث قال : الزبانية أرجلهم في الأرض ورؤوسهم في السماء

DURR:96:7/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:7/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:7/r8.claim: Qatada says the passage was revealed over Abu Jahl’s threat against Muhammad; Muhammad is the guided, pious one, Abu Jahl the denier, his council his people and clan, and al-zabaniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:7/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدوّ الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:7/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:7/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:7/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies Abu Jahl as forbidding Muhammad’s prayer, glosses his nadi as his clan, and says al-zabaniya are angels.
DURR:96:7/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل نهى محمداً إذا صلى { فليدع ناديه } قال : عشيرته { سندع الزبانية } قال : الملائكة

DURR:96:7/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:7/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن الحرث
DURR:96:7/r12.claim: Abdullah ibn al-Harith describes the zabaniya as having their feet on earth and their heads in heaven.
