DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.claim: The Prophet says that if Abu Jahl did this, the angels would seize him in plain sight.
DURR-FULL:v8p564/r1.anchor: فبلغ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: لو فعل لأخذته الملائكة عيانا

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.claim: Abu Jahl recoils from the Prophet, seeing a trench of fire and wings; the Prophet says angels would tear him limb from limb, and the final verses identify Abu Jahl's clan and the angels as his assembly and the zabaniya.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r1.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لو دنا مني لاختطفته الملائكة عضوا عضوا

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.claim: He says the passage was revealed about Abu Jahl's threat to trample Muhammad; the guided one is Muhammad, the denier is Abu Jahl, his assembly is his clan, and ‘zabaniya’ means police in Arabic.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.claim: He identifies Abu Jahl as the one stopping Muhammad from prayer, his assembly as his clan, and the zabaniya as angels.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد {أرأيت الذي ينهى عبدا إذا صلى} قال: أبو جهل نهى محمدا إذا صلى

DURR-FULL:v8p565/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r7.claim: He describes the zabaniya as beings whose feet are on earth and heads in heaven.
DURR-FULL:v8p565/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحرث قال: الزبانية أرجلهم في الأرض ورؤوسهم في السماء

FARRA:v1p91/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p91/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p91/r1.claim: Arabic can omit the plural wāw, relying on the preceding ḍamma; al-Farrāʾ cites سندع الزبانية, ويدع الإنسان and three poetic examples.
FARRA:v1p91/r1.anchor: وقد تسقط العرب الواو وهي واو جماع

TAB:96:17/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Abu Jahl threatened the Prophet while he prayed at the Maqām; God revealed the challenge, and the angels of punishment would seize Abu Jahl if he summoned his council.
TAB:96:17/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام

TAB:96:17/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r3.claim: In another report, Abu Jahl forbids the Prophet to pray and boasts of his council; after an unpreserved remark from the Prophet, Ibn Abbas says angels would seize Abu Jahl where he stood.
TAB:96:17/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي

TAB:96:17/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to kill Muhammad if he prayed again at the Maqām; the Prophet said battalions had darkened the space between them, and angels would seize Abu Jahl if he moved.
TAB:96:17/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه

TAB:96:17/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:96:17/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to step on the Prophet's neck at the Kaʿba; the Prophet said angels would take him in plain sight if he did.
TAB:96:17/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس ،   قال :  قال أبو جهل :  لئن رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند الكعبة

TAB:96:17/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r8.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:96:17/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies the zabāniya as angels.
TAB:96:17/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد {  سندع الزبانية } قال :  الملائكة

TAB:96:17/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي الهذيل
TAB:96:17/r9.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī al-Hudhayl describes the zabāniya as beings whose feet are on earth and heads in heaven.
TAB:96:17/r9.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبي الهذيل :  الزبانية أرجلهم في الأرض ،   ورؤوسهم في السماء

TAB:96:17/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r10.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:17/r10.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet's warning that, if Abu Jahl acted, the zabāniya angels would seize him visibly.
TAB:96:17/r10.anchor: عن قتادة ،   في قوله :  {  سندع الزبانية } قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «لو فعل أبو جهل لأخذته الزبانية الملائكة عيانا »

TAB:96:17/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r11.speaker: قتادة
TAB:96:17/r11.claim: Qatada glosses the zabāniya as angels.
TAB:96:17/r11.anchor: عن قتادة {  سندع الزبانية } قال :  الملائكة

TAB:96:17/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:96:17/r12.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:96:17/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the zabāniya as angels.
TAB:96:17/r12.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله :  الزبانية ،   قال :  الملائكة

THALABI:v1p91/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p91/r1.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v1p91/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet calls teachers the best people, urges that they be given support rather than burdened with hiring, and says teaching a child the basmala brings deliverance from the Fire for child, parents, and teacher.
THALABI:v1p91/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس (رضي الله عنه) قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «خير الناس وخير من يمشي على جديد الأرض المعلمون

THALABI:v1p91/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p91/r2.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v1p91/r2.claim: Jabir reports that when the basmala descended, clouds fled east, winds stilled, the sea surged, animals listened, devils were pelted from heaven, and God promised healing and blessing for anything named with it and Paradise for its reciter.
THALABI:v1p91/r2.anchor: عن عطاء عن جابر قال: (لما نزلت بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم هرب الغيم إلى المشرق، وسكنت الرياح، وهاج البحر

THALABI:v1p91/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v1p91/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v1p91/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says reciting the basmala can save a person from the nineteen zabaniya because it has nineteen letters, with a garden granted for each letter against one of them.
THALABI:v1p91/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: (من أراد أن ينجيه الله من الزبانية التسعة عشر فليقرأ بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم فإنها تسعة عشر حرفا

BURHAN:v1p397/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p397/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p397/r3.claim: The omitted waw in سندع signals swift action, the guards’ immediate response, forceful seizure, and a grave threat whose ending is elided.
BURHAN:v1p397/r3.anchor: أولها ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾ فيه سرعة الفعل وإجابة الزبانية وقوة البطش وهو وعيد عظيم ذكر مبدؤه وحذف آخره

BURHAN:v4p103/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p103/r5.speaker: يعقوب
BURHAN:v4p103/r5.claim: Yaqub pauses on the original waw in يمح, while other readers pause without it following the written form; omission is not jussive marking.
BURHAN:v4p103/r5.anchor: ولهذا وقف عليه يعقوب بالواو نظرا للاصل وان وقف عليه غيره بغير واو اتباعا للخط

BURHAN:v2p497/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p497/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p497/r5.claim: The omitted final waw in the pause forms is explained by pausing; Yaqub’s pause with the waw confirms this.
BURHAN:v2p497/r5.anchor: فللوقف ويؤكد ذلك وقوف يعقوب عليها بالواو

ITQAN:v1p239/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p239/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p239/r2.claim: Reported stop-spelling exceptions include adding wāw in yadʿu al-insān, yawm yadʿu al-dāʿ, and sanadʿu al-zabāniya, alongside specific hā, yā, alif, and joining conventions.
ITQAN:v1p239/r2.anchor: ﴿ ويدع الإنسان ﴾ ﴿ يوم يدع الداع ﴾ ﴿ سندع الزبانية ﴾

ITQAN:v4p447/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447/r1.claim: The omitted alif in “God effaces falsehood” suggests its rapid disappearance and annihilation.
ITQAN:v4p447/r1.anchor: وأما ( ويمح الله الباطل ) فللإشارة إلى سرعة ذهابه واضمحلاله

ITQAN:v4p447/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447/r2.claim: The omitted alif in “the caller calls” suggests the call’s speed and the speed with which those called answer.
ITQAN:v4p447/r2.anchor: وأما ( يدع الداع ) فللإشارة إلى سرعة الدعاء وسرعة إجابة المدعوين

ITQAN:v4p447/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p447/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p447/r3.claim: The omitted alif in “We will summon the guards” conveys swift action and response by the zabaniya and the severity of their force.
ITQAN:v4p447/r3.anchor: فللإشارة إلى سرعة الفعل وإجابة الزبانية وشدة البطش

NASHR:v1p456/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p456/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p456/r3.claim: Al-Makki’s prohibition on pausing at هاوم, based on an assumed original waw that would conflict with either spelling or etymology, is a clear error; every reader may pause on mīm.
NASHR:v1p456/r3.anchor: وهذا مما نبه عليه الأستاذ أبو شامة

NASHR:v1p456/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p456/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p456/r4.claim: The deleted waw in connected spellings such as سندع الزبانية illustrates that the plural mīm is paused on without restoring a waw, even for readers who join it in recitation.
NASHR:v1p456/r4.anchor: فما بعده ساكن أولى فالوقف على الميم لجميع القراء

NASHR:v2p140/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r3.speaker: جميع القراء
NASHR:v2p140/r3.claim: At the four words whose waw is omitted in the written form before a quiescent letter, all readers pause according to the rasm.
NASHR:v2p140/r3.anchor: وأما ما حذف من الواوات رسما للساكن، وهو أربعة مواضع ويدع الإنسان. في سبحان. ويمح الله الباطل

NASHR:v2p140/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r4.speaker: مكي وغيره
NASHR:v2p140/r4.claim: Makki and others advise against pausing on these forms or their analogues because either rasm or the underlying form would be violated.
NASHR:v2p140/r4.anchor: وقد قال مكي وغيره: لا ينبغي أن يعتمد الوقف عليها، ولا على ما يشابهها لأنه إن وقف بالرسم خالف الأصل

NASHR:v2p140/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p140/r5.claim: The author rejects that restriction: these are emergency stops, and where a transmitted reading is sound it is acceptable even if it departs from rasm or the underlying form.
NASHR:v2p140/r5.anchor: ولا يخفى ما فيه فإن الوقف على هذه وأشباهها ليس على وجه الاختيار والفرض أنه لو اضطر إلى الوقف عليها كيف يكون

NASHR:v2p140/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p140/r6.speaker: يعقوب عن أبي الفتح وأبي الحسن
NASHR:v2p140/r6.claim: Al-Dani transmits Yaqub pausing with waw according to the underlying form and says this was his reading from both teachers; Ibn al-Jazari notes it as an individual route he has read.
NASHR:v2p140/r6.anchor: وقد نص الحافظ أبو عمرو الداني عن يعقوب على الوقف عليها بالواو على الأصل

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r8.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r8.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r8.claim: Ibn Hisham defines zabāniya as harsh, strong ones and says that in this verse they are the keepers of Hell.
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r8.anchor: والزبانية: الغلاظ الشداد، وهم في هذا الموضع: خزنة النار

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r9.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r9.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r9.claim: In worldly usage zabāniya can mean a man's helpers; Ibn al-Ziba'ra's line calls stout, powerful helpers zabāniya.
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r9.anchor: مطاعيم في المقرى مطاعين في الوغى

IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r10.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r10.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r10.claim: Sakhr al-Ghay's line also uses zabāniya for a retinue of men, supporting the word's worldly sense.
IBNHISHAM:v1p311#3/r10.anchor: قال صخر بن عبد الله الهذلي، وهو صخر الغي: ومن كبير نفر زبانيه

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r1.claim: Al-zabāniya are the angels of punishment.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r1.anchor: الزبانية : ملائكة العذاب ،   فقيل : جمع لا واحد لهمن لفظه

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r2.claim: One view treats zabāniya as a plural with no singular from the same form, like ʿabādīd.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r2.anchor: فقيل : جمع لا واحد لهمن لفظه ،   كعباديد

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r3.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives zabniya as its singular, on the patterns of ḥadriya and ʿafriya.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r3.anchor: وقيل : واحدهم زبنية على وزن حدرية وعفرية ،   قاله أبو عبيدة

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r4.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r4.claim: Al-Kisāʾī gives zabnī as the singular, deriving it from zabn by altered nisba formation, like ansī from its underlying form.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r4.anchor: وقال الكسائي : زبني ،   وكأنه نسب إلى الزبن ثم غير للنسب ،   كقولهم : أنسي

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r5.speaker: عيسى بن عمرو الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r5.claim: Al-Akhfash gives zābin as the singular; Arabs also use the name for someone of forceful violence.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r5.anchor: قال عيسى بن عمرو الأخفش : واحدهم زابن ،   والعرب تطلق هذا الاسم على من اشتد بطشه

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r6.claim: An unnamed poet uses zabana for war violently seizing someone, illustrating the word’s association with force.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r6.anchor: قول الشاعر : ومستعجب مما يرى من أناتنا *** ولو زبنته الحرب لم يترمرم

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r7.speaker: عتبة بن أبي سفيان
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r7.claim: ʿUtba ibn Abī Sufyān likewise uses the verb for war overcoming people and their overcoming it.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r7.anchor: وقال عتبة بن أبي سفيان : وقد زنبتنا الحرب وزبناها

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r8.claim: The majority read sanadʿu in the active voice with nūn; the written wāw is omitted because it drops in connected speech when two sukūns meet.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { سندع } بالنون مبنياً للفاعل ،   وكتبت بغير واو لأنها تسقط في الوصل لالتقاء الساكنين

ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r9.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r9.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads sayudʿā in the passive, with al-zabāniya in the nominative.
ABUHAYYAN:96:18/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة : سيدعى مبنياً للمفعول الزبانيه رفع

ALUSI:96:18/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:18/r1.claim: Al-zabāniya are the angels of punishment who drag him into Hell; the word originally named guards or assistants of rulers.
ALUSI:96:18/r1.anchor: أي ملائكة العذاب ليجروه إلى النار وهو في الأصل الشرط أي أعوان الولاة

ALUSI:96:18/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r2.speaker: أبو عبيد
ALUSI:96:18/r2.claim: The word may have no singular from its own form, like ʿabābīd; Abū ʿUbayd gives zabniyya as its singular, while al-Kisāʾī gives zabnī and relates it to pushing.
ALUSI:96:18/r2.anchor: فقيل جمع لا واحد له من لفظه كعباديد وقال أبو عبيد واحده زبنية

ALUSI:96:18/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر والأخفش
ALUSI:96:18/r3.claim: ʿĪsā b. ʿUmar and al-Akhfash give zābin as the singular; another derivation starts from zabānī and deletes a yāʾ, compensating with tāʾ.
ALUSI:96:18/r3.anchor: وقال عيسى بن عمر والأخفش واحده زابن والعرب قد تطلق هذا الاسم

ALUSI:96:18/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:18/r4.claim: Arabic also calls forceful people zabāniya even when they are not officials' assistants; the cited poetry describes mighty fighters by the term.
ALUSI:96:18/r4.anchor: والعرب قد تطلق هذا الاسم على من اشتد بطشه وإن لم يكن من أعوان الولاة

ALUSI:96:18/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:18/r5.claim: The punishing angels are called zabāniya because they push those they punish into the Fire.
ALUSI:96:18/r5.anchor: وسمى ملائكة العذاب بذلك لدفعهم من يعذبونه إلى النار

ALUSI:96:18/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:18/r6.claim: The threat may operate in this world: a report says that if Abū Jahl called his council, the angels would seize him visibly.
ALUSI:96:18/r6.anchor: وهذا الدعاء في الدنيا بناءً على ما روي من أنه لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عياناً

ALUSI:96:18/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:18/r7.claim: Sanadʿu is indicative because no subjunctive or jussive particle governs it; the written omission of wāw follows connected pronunciation after sukūn or parallels yadʿu in the preceding verse.
ALUSI:96:18/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن سندع مرفوع لتجرده عن الناصب والجازم

ALUSI:96:18/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:96:18/r8.claim: Some say sanadʿu is jussive as the response to the command, but al-Ālūsī considers that analysis weak.
ALUSI:96:18/r8.anchor: وقيل إنه مجزوم في جواب الأمر وفيه نظر

ALUSI:96:18/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:96:18/r9.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI:96:18/r9.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads sayudʿā al-zabāniya in the passive, with al-zabāniya nominative.
ALUSI:96:18/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة سيدعي الزبانية بالبناء للمفعول ورفع الزبانية

BAGHAWI:96:18/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:96:18/r1.claim: Zabāniya is plural of zabnī and derives from zabn, meaning pushing or repelling.
BAGHAWI:96:18/r1.anchor: جمع زبني ، مأخوذ من الزبن ، وهو الدفع

BAGHAWI:96:18/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:96:18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as the keepers of Hell, named for pushing Hell’s inhabitants into it.
BAGHAWI:96:18/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يريد زبانية جهنم ، سموا بها لأنهم يدفعون أهل النار إليها

BAGHAWI:96:18/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:18/r3.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI:96:18/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the zabāniya are harsh, powerful angels.
BAGHAWI:96:18/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : هم الملائكة الغلاظ الشداد

BAGHAWI:96:18/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:96:18/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI:96:18/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas warns that if Abu Jahl calls his assembly, God’s zabāniya will seize him.
BAGHAWI:96:18/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لو دعا ناديه لأخذته زبانية الله

BAYDAWI:96:18/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:18/r1.claim: A report says Abu Jahl passed the Prophet while he prayed, claimed he had more supporters in the valley, and the verse came down about summoning the guards to drag him to the Fire.
BAYDAWI:96:18/r1.anchor: روي أنا أبا جهل لعنه الله مر برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يصلي فقال : ألم أنهك

BAYDAWI:96:18/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:18/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:18/r2.claim: The summoned zabāniya are to drag the threatened man into the Fire.

BAYDAWI:96:18/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:96:18/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:96:18/r3.claim: Zabāniya are guards; their singular is zabniyya, like ʿifrīya, from pushing, or zabnī by relation, with tāʾ replacing the original yāʾ.
BAYDAWI:96:18/r3.anchor: وهو في الأصل الشرط ، واحدها زبنية كعفرية من الزبن وهو الدفع ، أو زبني على النسب وأصلها زباني والتاء معوضة عن الياء

BIQAI:96:18/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:18/r1.claim: In answer to the implied question about the result of summoning his gathering, God promises to summon the zabāniya, the guards who drag him to Hell.

BIQAI:96:18/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:18/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:18/r2.claim: Zabāniya originally refers to guards or police, singular zabniya, from zabn meaning to push; alternatively it is a nisba form, with tāʾ replacing yāʾ; they are large and powerful.
BIQAI:96:18/r2.anchor: وهم في الأصل الشرط ،   الواحد زبنية كهبرية

BIQAI:96:18/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:18/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:18/r3.claim: The ʿUthmānic codices all omit the wāw in the written form of the verb, although Arabic gives no phonetic reason for its omission.
BIQAI:96:18/r3.anchor: وقد اجتمعت المصاحف العثمانية على حذف الواو من هذا الفعل خطأ

BIQAI:96:18/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:18/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:18/r4.claim: Biqāʿī tentatively explains the omitted wāw as preventing any belief that the angels have independent elevated power; all strength belongs to God, the Mighty.
BIQAI:96:18/r4.anchor: أن لا يظن أنهم دعوا لرفعة لهم في ذواتهم يستعان بهم بسببها

BIQAI:96:18/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:18/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:18/r5.claim: He also suggests that the spelling resembles an imperative, signaling an inevitable summons and response, perfectly matching script and meaning, with the prefixed sīn reinforcing certainty and establishment.
BIQAI:96:18/r5.anchor: إن الحذف دال على تشبيه الفعل بالأمر ليدل على أن هذا الدعاء أمر

BIQAI:96:18/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:96:18/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI:96:18/r6.claim: Alternatively, the lightest summons suffices to unleash an irresistible force; the angels would be even more overwhelming if their summons were strengthened.
BIQAI:96:18/r6.anchor: إنا ندعوهم بأيسر دعاء وأسهل أمر

DURR:96:17/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Abū Jahl’s threat to trample Muhammad’s neck at the Kaʿba; the Prophet said angels would seize him in plain sight if he did.
DURR:96:17/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت محمداً يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن عنقه

DURR:96:17/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Abū Jahl confronted the Prophet at prayer, boasted of having the largest council, and the verses answered that his council and God’s angels would be summoned; Abū Jahl would be seized.
DURR:96:17/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي ، فجاء أبو جهل فقال

DURR:96:17/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:96:17/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Abū Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the Maqām; when asked why he did not act, the Prophet said the space between them had darkened, and angels would seize him if he moved.
DURR:96:17/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه

DURR:96:17/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r5.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
DURR:96:17/r5.claim: Al-ʿAbbās says Abū Jahl vowed to trample the Prophet while prostrating; when Muhammad recited the sūra, Abū Jahl said the sky’s horizon was blocked from him, and Muhammad prostrated at its end.
DURR:96:17/r5.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب قال : كنت يوماً في المسجد فأقبل أبو جهل

DURR:96:17/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:96:17/r6.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that Abū Jahl recoiled from the praying Prophet, describing a trench of fire and wings between them; Muhammad said angels would tear him limb from limb if he approached.
DURR:96:17/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه إلا بين أظهركم ؟

DURR:96:17/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR:96:17/r7.claim: In Abū Hurayra’s report, the condemned man is Abū Jahl, his “council” is his people, and the zabāniya are angels.
DURR:96:17/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه إلا بين أظهركم ؟

DURR:96:17/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r9.speaker: قتادة
DURR:96:17/r9.claim: Qatāda says the passage was revealed over Abū Jahl’s threat against Muhammad: the guided man is Muhammad, the denier is Abū Jahl, his council is his people and clan, and zabāniya means police in Arabic.
DURR:96:17/r9.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله : { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : نزلت في عدو الله أبي جهل

DURR:96:17/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r10.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:96:17/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies the forbidding man as Abū Jahl, his nadi as his clan, and the zabāniya as angels.
DURR:96:17/r10.anchor: عن مجاهد { أرأيت الذي ينهى عبداً إذا صلى } قال : أبو جهل نهى محمداً إذا صلى

DURR:96:17/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:17/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن الحرث
DURR:96:17/r13.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith describes the zabāniya as having feet on earth and heads in heaven.
DURR:96:17/r13.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحرث قال : الزبانية أرجلهم في الأرض ورؤوسهم في السماء .

DURR:96:18/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR:96:18/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the seeker of knowledge and the seeker of worldly gain are both insatiable: knowledge brings God’s approval, while wealth-seeking leads to transgression.
DURR:96:18/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال : منهومان لا يشبعان : صاحب علم وصاحب دنيا

DURR:96:18/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:96:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس

IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.claim: Al-Tirmidhī and al-Nasāʾī transmit Ibn ʿAbbās's report: Abū Jahl confronted the Prophet praying at the Maqām, threatened him, claimed the valley's largest assembly, and the two verses exposed his intent to summon supporters against him.
IBNASHUR:96:17/r1.anchor: ومناسبة ذلك ما رواه الترمذي والنسائي عن ابن عباس قال :  « كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل

IBNASHUR:96:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:18/r1.claim: Sanadʿu answers the challenging imperative and is jussive; its written form omits the final wāw, while the future marker reinforces the force of the action.
IBNASHUR:96:18/r1.anchor: وقوله :  { سندع الزبانية } جواب الأمر التعجيزي ،  أي فإن دعا ناديه دعونا لهم الزبانية ففعل { سندع } مجزوم في جواب الأمر

IBNASHUR:96:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:18/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:18/r2.claim: Zabāniya has several proposed plural forms—of zabānī, zibniya, or zibnī—or may be a collective with no singular of the same form.
IBNASHUR:96:18/r2.anchor: والزبانية :  بفتح الزاي وتخفيف التحتية جمع زباني بفتح الزاي وبتحتية مشددة ،  أو جمع زبنية بكسر الزاي

IBNASHUR:96:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:18/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:18/r3.claim: The word derives from zabn, forceful pushing: a zabūn camel kicks its milker and a zabūn war involves repeated pushing in combat; the zabāniya are punitive angels and the term also names police assistants.
IBNASHUR:96:18/r3.anchor: فالزبانية الذين يزبنون الناس ،  أي يدفعونهم بشدة .  والمراد بهم ملائكة العذاب

IBNASHUR:96:19/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:96:19/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:96:19/r2.claim: The muṣḥaf writes sanadʿ without a wāw after the ʿayn to reflect connected recitation, since the word is neither a pause point nor an end-rhyme.
IBNASHUR:96:19/r2.anchor: وكتب { سندع } في المصحف بدون واو بعد العين مراعاة لحالة الوصل ،  لأنها ليست محل وقف ولا فاصلة

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r1.claim: The zabāniya are angels of punishment who push people into Hell; zabn means pushing.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r1.anchor: وهم الذين يدفعون الناس في النار ، والزبن : الدفع

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r2.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r2.claim: Al-Kisaʾi gives zabni as a singular form of zabāniya.

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r3.speaker: عيسى بن عمر الأخفش
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r3.claim: Isa ibn Umar al-Akhfash gives zābin as a singular form.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r3.anchor: وقال عيسى بن عمر الأخفش : " زابن "

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r4.claim: War is called zabūn because it pushes people around.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r4.anchor: ومنه " حرب زبون " أي تدفع الناس في نفسها

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r5.claim: A poet uses the verb zabana for the war's pushing; the line says the patient would not stir if war shoved him.

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r6.speaker: عتبة بن أبي سفيان
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r6.claim: Utba ibn Abi Sufyan says war pushed them and they pushed it, calling themselves its children and it their mother.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r6.anchor: ومنه قول عتبة بن أبي سفيان : " وقد زبنتنا الحرب وزبناها ، فنحن بنوها وهي أمنا "

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r7.claim: Another poem calls a war zabūn, one that pushes people and keeps visitors apart.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r7.anchor: عدتني عن زيارتك العوادي *** وحالت بيننا حرب زبون

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r8.claim: The written muṣḥaf omits the wāw in sanadʿu for abbreviation and lightening.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r8.anchor: وحذفت الواو من [ سندع ] في خط المصحف اختصارا وتخفيفا

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r9.claim: God will summon the zabāniya to punish the man who calls his council.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r9.anchor: والمعنى : سندعو الزبانية لعذاب هذا الذي يدعو ناديه

IBNATIYYA:96:18/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r10.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r10.claim: Ibn Masud reads fal-yadʿu ilā nādīhi, adding ilā.
IBNATIYYA:96:18/r10.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود : ( فليدع إلى ناديه )

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r1.claim: The zabāniya are the angels of punishment; the contest will show whether God's party or Abu Jahl's party prevails.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r1.anchor: وهم ملائكة العذاب ، حتى يعلم من يغلب : أحزبنا أو حزبه

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Abu Jahl's threat to trample the Prophet's neck at the Kaaba; the Prophet warned that angels would seize him if he did.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت محمدا يصلي عند الكعبة لأطأن على عنقه

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.claim: In another Ibn Abbas report, Abu Jahl threatens the Prophet at the Maqam and boasts of his large council; Ibn Abbas says angels would seize the council immediately. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي عند المقام فمر به أبو جهل بن هشام

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits Abu Jahl's threat to step on the Prophet's neck; the Prophet says angels would seize him in plain sight, then mentions the fate of Jews wishing for death and those who left for mutual imprecation.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن رأيت رسول الله يصلي عند الكعبة لآتينه حتى أطأ على عنقه

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r5.claim: A further Ibn Abbas version says Abu Jahl threatened to kill Muhammad at the Maqam; revelation followed, and Abu Jahl saw battalions between them. Ibn Abbas says angels would seize him if he moved.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال أبو جهل : لئن عاد محمد يصلي عند المقام لأقتلنه

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that Abu Jahl recoiled from the praying Prophet, seeing a fiery trench, dread, and wings; the Prophet said angels would seize him limb by limb.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال : قال أبو جهل : هل يعفر محمد وجهه بين أظهركم

IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir is unsure whether Abu Hurayra's report itself says that the passage from 96:6 through the end of the sura was revealed.
IBNKATHIR:96:18/r7.anchor: وأنزل الله - لا أدري في حديث أبي هريرة أم لا - :

MAWARDI:96:18/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:18/r1.claim: The zabaniya are angels who guard Hell; they are exceptionally large and forceful, and Arabs use the word for anyone of great might.
MAWARDI:96:18/r1.anchor: والزبانية هم الملائكة من خزنة جهنم ، وهم أعظم الملائكة خلقاً وأشدهم بطشاً

MAWARDI:96:18/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:96:18/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:96:18/r2.claim: The cited anonymous poem calls fierce, mighty people zabaniya, supporting the word's association with strength.
MAWARDI:96:18/r2.anchor: والعرب تطلق هذا الاسم على من اشتد بطشه ، قال الشاعر : مطاعيم في القصوى مطاعين في الوغى

NASAFI:96:17/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:17/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:96:17/r3.claim: Zabāniya is the language's term for a guard or enforcer, singular zabniyya, from pushing; it refers here to the angels of punishment.
NASAFI:96:17/r3.anchor: والزبانية لغة الشرط الواحد زبنية من الزبن وهو الدفع

NASAFI:96:17/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:17/r4.speaker: عنه عليه السلام
NASAFI:96:17/r4.claim: The Prophet said that if Abū Jahl called his gathering, the angels of punishment would seize him in plain sight.
NASAFI:96:17/r4.anchor: وعنه عليه السلام " لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية عياناً

NASAFI:96:18/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:96:18/r3.speaker: author

QURTUBI:96:17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
QURTUBI:96:17/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others identify the zabāniya as stern, powerful angels.
QURTUBI:96:17/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس وغيره - واحدهم زبني

QURTUBI:96:17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r3.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI:96:17/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī gives zabnī as the singular form of zabāniya.

QURTUBI:96:17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r4.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI:96:17/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash gives zābin as the singular form of zabāniya.
QURTUBI:96:17/r4.anchor: وقال الأخفش : زابن .   أبو عبيدة : زبنية

QURTUBI:96:17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI:96:17/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda gives zabniya as the singular form.

QURTUBI:96:17/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:17/r6.claim: Another proposed singular is zabānī; another analysis treats the word as a collective plural like abābīl or ʿabādīd.
QURTUBI:96:17/r6.anchor: وقيل : زباني .   وقيل : هو اسم للجمع ،   كالأبابيل والعباديد

QURTUBI:96:17/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r7.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI:96:17/r7.claim: In Arab usage the zabāniya are the police.
QURTUBI:96:17/r7.anchor: وقال قتادة : هم الشرط في كلام العرب

QURTUBI:96:17/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:17/r8.claim: The word derives from zabn, pushing; the sale called muzābana shares this root.

QURTUBI:96:17/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r9.speaker: أبو الليث السمرقندي
QURTUBI:96:17/r9.claim: One explanation says they are called zabāniya because they work with their feet as they do with their hands.
QURTUBI:96:17/r9.anchor: وقيل : إنما سموا الزبانية لأنهم يعملون بأرجلهم ،   كما يعملون بأيديهم

QURTUBI:96:17/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:17/r10.claim: A report says Abu Jahl boasted he would summon his people after hearing the threat to seize his forelock; hearing of the zabāniya frightened him, and he claimed to have seen a threatening horseman.
QURTUBI:96:17/r10.anchor: وروي في الخبر أن النبي صلى اللّه عليه وسلم لما قرأ هذه السورة

QURTUBI:96:17/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r11.speaker: الأخبار
QURTUBI:96:17/r11.claim: Reports picture the zabāniya with heads in the sky and feet on earth, pushing unbelievers into Hell.
QURTUBI:96:17/r11.anchor: وفي الأخبار أن الزبانية رؤوسهم في السماء وأرجلهم في الأرض ،   فهم يدفعون الكفار في جهنم

QURTUBI:96:17/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:96:17/r12.claim: Another view says they are the largest angels in creation and the strongest in force.
QURTUBI:96:17/r12.anchor: وقيل : إنهم أعظم الملائكة خلقا ،   وأشدهم بطشا

QURTUBI:96:17/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI:96:17/r13.claim: Arabs also use zabāniya for anyone whose force is formidable.
QURTUBI:96:17/r13.anchor: والعرب تطلق هذا الاسم على من اشتد بطشه

QURTUBI:96:17/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:96:17/r14.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:96:17/r14.claim: The poet’s description of leaders as zabāniya supports the word’s use for people of formidable strength.
QURTUBI:96:17/r14.anchor: مطاعيمُ في القُصْوَى مطاعينُ في الوَغَى*** زبانيةٌ غُلْب عِطَامٌ حُلُومُهَا

QURTUBI:96:17/r15.speaker: ابن عباس

QURTUBI:96:17/r15.anchor: وعن عكرمة عن ابن عباس : " سندع الزبانية " قال : قال أبو جهل

QURTUBI:96:17/r16.anchor: وروى عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال : مر أبو جهل على النبي

RAZI:96:16/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r3.speaker: أبو جهل
RAZI:96:16/r3.claim: After Muhammad spoke sharply and recited the verses, Abu Jahl boasted that he had the largest assembly in the valley; the following threat to summon angels answered his boast.
RAZI:96:16/r3.anchor: قال : يا محمد بمن تهددني وأني لأكثر هذا الوادي ناديا ، فافتخر بجماعته الذين كانوا يأكلون حطامه ، فنزل قوله تعالى : { فليدع ناديه سندع الزبانية }

RAZI:96:16/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والمبرد
RAZI:96:16/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayda and al-Mubarrad give zabniya as the singular of zabāniya, from a root meaning to push; it can describe a rebellious human or jinn, like ʿifriya.
RAZI:96:16/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة والمبرد : واحد الزبانية زبنية

RAZI:96:16/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r7.speaker: الأخفش
RAZI:96:16/r7.claim: Al-Akhfash reports proposed singular forms zabānī and zābin; another view treats zabāniya as a plural without a singular of that form, like abābīl and ʿabādīd.
RAZI:96:16/r7.anchor: وقال الأخفش : قال بعضهم واحده الزباني

RAZI:96:16/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r8.claim: The zabāniya are angels of punishment, distinguished by formidable strength.
RAZI:96:16/r8.anchor: وبالجملة فالمراد ملائكة العذاب ، ولا شك أنهم مخصوصون بقوة شديدة

RAZI:96:16/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r9.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:96:16/r9.claim: Muqātil describes them as Hell's keepers, with feet on earth and heads in heaven.
RAZI:96:16/r9.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هم خزنة جهنم أرجلهم في الأرض ورؤسهم في السماء

RAZI:96:16/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r10.speaker: قتادة
RAZI:96:16/r10.claim: Qatāda says zabāniya means police in Arabic; these are stern, harsh angels called so because they shove unbelievers into Hell.
RAZI:96:16/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة : الزبانية هم الشرط في كلام العرب

RAZI:96:16/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r11.claim: One reading challenges Abu Jahl to call his allies against Muhammad: God will summon angels beyond the assembly's power.
RAZI:96:16/r11.anchor: ( الأول ) : أي فليفعل ما ذكره من أنه يدعو أنصاره

RAZI:96:16/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:96:16/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that if Abu Jahl called his assembly, the angels would seize him immediately, in full view.
RAZI:96:16/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس : لو دعا ناديه لأخذته الزبانية

RAZI:96:16/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r13.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r13.claim: Another explanation says the threat foretells Abu Jahl being dragged like a dog in this life, as happened at Badr.
RAZI:96:16/r13.anchor: وقيل : هذا إخبار من الله تعالى بأنه يجر في الدنيا

RAZI:96:16/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r14.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r14.claim: A further explanation places the angels' dragging of Abu Jahl into Hell in the afterlife.
RAZI:96:16/r14.anchor: وقيل : بل هذا إخبار بأن الزبانية يجرونه في الآخرة إلى النار

RAZI:96:16/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:16/r15.speaker: author
RAZI:96:16/r15.claim: A second interpretation rearranges the sequence: God seizes the forelock and summons angels in the afterlife, then Abu Jahl calls his assembly to protect him.
RAZI:96:16/r15.anchor: ( القول الثاني ) : أن في الآية تقديما وتأخيرا أي لنسفعا بالناصية

RAZI:96:18/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:18/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:96:18/r1.claim: A passive reading, ستدعى, is reported for the phrase.
RAZI:96:18/r1.anchor: المسألة الخامسة : قرئ : { ستدعى } على المجهول

RAZI:96:18/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:18/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:96:18/r2.claim: The future sīn does not express doubt: God's promise is certain, especially the assurance that He will avenge the Prophet on his enemy.
RAZI:96:18/r2.anchor: وهذه السين ليست للشك فإن عسى من الله واجب الوقوع

RAZI:96:18/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:96:18/r3.speaker: النبي
RAZI:96:18/r3.claim: Razi connects the future wording to the Prophet's assurance: “I will help you, even after a time.”
RAZI:96:18/r3.anchor: ولعل فائدة السين هو المراد من قوله عليه السلام : «لأنصرنك ولو بعد حين »
